title: A Study of BI 4015092, Alone or in Combination With Other Cancer Treatment, in Patients With Advanced Cancer That Has a KRAS G12D Mutation
official: Open-label, Multicenter, First-in-human Trial to Explore Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Preliminary Efficacy of BI 4015092 as Monotherapy and as Combination Therapy in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors With KRAS G12D Mutation
summary:
This study is for adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumours, including colorectal cancer and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. People who have a tumour that has a KRAS G12D gene mutation can take part. This study is open for people for whom other treatment may not have worked or may not be suitable. The purpose of this study is to find out how well a new study medicine called BI 4015092 is tolerated and how it affects these tumours when used alone and together with another medicine called cetuximab. This is the first time BI 4015092 is given to humans.

This study has 4 parts. In all parts, participants receive BI 4015092, either alone or together with cetuximab.

* In Part A1, small groups of participants receive BI 4015092 alone, and the dose is slowly increased to find a suitable dose that people can tolerate.
* In Part A2, participants receive BI 4015092 alone at a selected dose to further check how well people tolerate it and to look for early signs that it can stop tumours from growing or make them shrink.
* In Part B1, participants receive BI 4015092 together with cetuximab, and the dose of BI 4015092 is slowly increased to find a suitable dose for the combination.
* In Part B2, participants receive BI 4015092 together with cetuximab. In this part, participants are put into groups by chance, like drawing names from a hat, and each group gets a different dose of BI 4015092 with cetuximab.

Participants can stay in the study as long as they benefit from the treatment and can tolerate it. During this time, they visit the study site regularly. At these visits, study doctors check participants' health and collect information about any health problems. They also regularly check the size of the tumours and whether the cancer has spread to other parts of the body.
conditions: Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors With KRAS G12D Mutation
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Age ≥18 years of age, or over the legal age of consent as required by local legislation.
2. Signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to any trial-specific procedures, sampling, or analyses.
3. Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors with the Kirsten rat sarcoma virus (KRAS) G12D mutation detected by a local test.

   1. Dose escalation monotherapy: Patients with advanced (metastatic or unresectable) KRAS G12D mutant solid tumor who have received and failed standard of care therapies or are intolerant to, or ineligible for, approved therapies.
   2. Dose escalation combination therapy: Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced (metastatic or unresectable) KRAS G12D mutant colorectal cancer (CRC), who have received and failed standard of care therapy or are intolerant to, or ineligible for, approved therapies.
   3. Monotherapy Expansion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cohort: Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced (metastatic or unresectable) KRAS G12D mutant PDAC who have received and progressed or experienced disease recurrence on or after at least one prior line of standard of care chemotherapy for advanced/metastatic disease. Prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant systemic therapy may be considered a prior line for eligibility only if the patient progressed during or within 6 months of completing the therapy. CRC Cohort: Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced (metastatic or unresectable) KRAS G12D mutant CRC, who have received and progressed or experienced disease recurrence on or after at least one prior line of standard of care chemotherapy for metastatic disease including a fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and/or irinotecan-based chemotherapy, unless the patient refused or was ineligible for such therapy.
   4. Combination dose optimization: Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced (metastatic or unresectable) KRAS G12D mutant CRC, who have received and progressed or experienced disease recurrence on or after at least one prior line of standard of care chemotherapy for metastatic disease including a fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and/or irinotecan-based chemotherapy, unless the patient refused or was ineligible for such therapy.
4. Participants must be willing to undergo a tumor biopsy at screening/baseline, if medically feasible, unless archival tissue was collected within 3 months before trial entry and the patient has not received treatment since the most recent biopsy. Archival tissue is acceptable if biopsy is not medically feasible. In backfill cohorts in the monotherapy dose escalation part, on-treatment biopsies are mandatory and end-of-treatment biopsies are optional; in all other parts of the trial, on-treatment and end-of-treatment biopsies are optional.
5. Further inclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion criteria:

1. Previous anticancer chemotherapy or targeted therapy within 3 weeks or immunotherapy within 4 weeks of the first administration of trial medicine.
2. Patients who had previous treatment with KRAS G12D inhibitor or (K)RAS/Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) targeting agents.
3. Known history of hypersensitivity to any of the excipients of BI 4015092 tablets and/or cetuximab.
4. History or presence of cardiovascular abnormalities such as uncontrolled hypertension (defined as: Blood pressure (BP) measured in a rested and relaxed condition, where systolic BP ≥140 mmHg, or diastolic BP ≥90 mmHg, with or without medication), congestive heart failure New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification of ≥III or IV, unstable angina or uncontrolled arrhythmia which are considered as clinically relevant by the investigator. History of myocardial infarction, stroke or pulmonary embolism within 6 months prior to randomization.
5. Further exclusion criteria apply.
